releases.name: v0.4.6 — One comment for one defect at several places
releases.body:
# Azure DevOps PR Review for OpenCode — 0.4.6

One defect that a pull request makes at several places now gets one inline
comment that lists the other places, where each place had a thread of its
own. The reviewer and verifier instructions are those of 0.4.5, so a review
finds and verifies as before; the comment planner's instructions changed, and
no setting is new.

## What changed

- **One comment for one defect at several places.** A mistake repeated in a
  pull request (the same wrong call in each handler, the same stale text in
  each copy) is one finding per place, because each place needs its own
  correction. Each of them used to get an inline thread with much the same
  text. The comment planner may now write one comment for such findings, at
  the place that shows the mistake most clearly.
- **Every other place is listed under it.** AZPR adds the list itself, from
  the findings' own locations:

  ```text
  **📍 Also at** (the same defect; fix these places with it):
  - `/src/orders/refund.ts:41-44` (F-3)
  - `/src/orders/cancel.ts:18` (F-5)
  ```

  In Chinese the heading is `**📍 其他位置**`. The list is plain text: nothing
  is collapsed or linked, so its own markup holds nothing back in automatic
  publication (a file name is checked like any other text of the comment).
  Azure DevOps cannot anchor one thread at several places, which is why the
  places are written out.
- **Only for the same defect.** Findings share a comment only when they have
  the same severity (high or medium), lie on different lines of files the
  pull request changes, and the planner says they are the same mistake with
  the same correction. Places that need different corrections keep their own
  comments, and when unsure the planner keeps findings apart. The preview
  shows a shared comment with all its findings and the planner's reason
  (`Combined: …`), so with a preview you see it before anything is posted
  (automatic publication, `afterReview: publish` or `--publish` after the PR
  URL, posts such a comment like any other). A place is
  listed as its finding states it, so only a finding whose lines the file
  has at the reviewed commit can be one of several places, and the comment's
  anchor must touch the lines of exactly one of its findings.
- **The review keeps every finding.** It still has one finding per place.
  Each keeps its row in the summary index and its ID, and you can leave one
  out or change its severity after a preview like any finding; the next
  preview then lists the places that are left.
- **One more planner stage on larger reviews.** Which findings may be such
  repeats is settled before the planning pages are made, and only when at
  least two high or medium findings of one severity lie at different places.
  When all findings fit one page (at most four, within a page's text), no
  session is added: that page is offered those findings. Otherwise, where
  two of them fit one page together, a grouping pass runs first: one more
  stage of the comment planner's model, usually one request, whose input is
  those findings and which says which are one mistake at several places. If
  it fails, a progress notice says so and the comments are planned one per
  place, as before.
- **"Already there" is exact.** Every inline comment ends with a hidden
  marker made of its file and the lines it quotes, and publication skips a
  comment whose marker the pull request already has. A shared comment's
  marker is also made of the other places it lists, so it is skipped only
  when this very comment, with every place, is there. The markers of
  comments for one place are unchanged, and so is publication.
- **No second thread on the same lines.** A shared comment and a comment for
  one place (a thread per place that an earlier version posted, say) do not
  find each other, so one would be posted next to the other. When planning,
  such a comment is sent back, and the planner is asked to put it at another
  place or to skip the finding a

releases.name: v0.4.5 — Stopping a run from the terminal panel
releases.body:
# Azure DevOps PR Review for OpenCode — 0.4.5

While a run is under way, the panel beside the conversation now offers to
stop it, so the command and the run's ID need not be found in the
conversation and typed. The reviewer, verifier and comment-planning
instructions are those of 0.4.4, and no setting is new.

## What changed

- **A run is stopped from the panel.** A `STARTED` notice says how its run is
  stopped (`/pr-stop <run-id>`), but in the conversation, with an ID to copy.
  While a run is under way (a review, a preview that is being planned, a
  publication, a check) the row at the panel's foot now offers one step:

  ```text
  [s] Stop this run…
  ```

  Click it, or press `s` while the panel has the keyboard. After the run's
  receipt the row shows what that receipt offers, as before: the steps of a
  preview, or nothing.
- **Stopping asks first.** The question's first row is "No, let it run", and
  it names the run. "Yes, stop it" sends `/pr-stop` with that run's ID to the
  session on screen, and AZPR takes it like a typed command: the run ends
  with its `CANCELLED` receipt. Requests that were already sent may still be
  billed, as with the typed command. What you type into the question finds a
  row by the beginning of its title (`y`, `n`), so `s` pressed once more than
  meant leaves no row for Enter to take; the question before posting answers
  the same way.
- **Only the run you were asked about is stopped.** An answer is acted on
  only while the panel still shows that run as under way. If it has ended, or
  the next run has started (the preview that follows a review by itself, for
  instance), while the question was open, nothing is sent and the panel says
  so. A step that reaches AZPR after its run has ended stops nothing, and no
  other run.
- **A run that has ended is not waited for.** Where the panel has no report or
  preview to show, it said "No report or preview yet." also of a run that had
  ended, such as one that was stopped. Once the run has its receipt it now
  says "This run ended with no report or preview to show."
- **A click on a step is not lost.** Since 0.4.4 the steps at the panel's foot
  were drawn anew whenever the panel worked its content out again, and a
  press or a release that came before the next frame went nowhere: now and
  then a click did nothing, most likely right after a notice arrived. Each
  step now keeps its element.

The step needs OpenCode's terminal UI. Other clients, such as the desktop
app, show AZPR's notices as before, and `/pr-stop` is typed as before. That a
run can be stopped travels with its `STARTED` notice as data no model reads;
the text of every notice is unchanged. See the
[terminal panel](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.4.5/README.md#terminal-panel).

## Installation

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-azure-devops-pr-review@0.4.5
```

Alternatively, install the same release from Git:

```sh
opencode plugin add 'github:WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2#v0.4.5'
```

Add only one of them. Then open OpenCode's terminal UI and type `/pr-setup`;
the
[quickstart](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.4.5/docs/QUICKSTART.md)
walks through it, with a recording of the dialogs, and shows the way without
the terminal UI.

## Upgrading AZPR

For an entry that `opencode plugin add` created, add 0.4.5 and remove the
previous version only when the download succeeded. Replace `PREVIOUS_VERSION`
with the version in your `plugins` entry, such as 0.4.4:

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-azure-devops-pr-review@0.4.5 &&
  opencode plugin remove opencode-azure-devops-pr-review@PREVIOUS_VERSION
```

Run them when no AZPR command is running. Running only the first command
leaves the previous version running. For an entry with options, change only
its `package` value; the OpenCode service then downloads 0.4.5 with its own
network settings. See
[upgrading](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devop

releases.name: v0.4.4 — The next step in the terminal panel
releases.body:
# Azure DevOps PR Review for OpenCode — 0.4.4

After a comment preview, the panel beside the conversation now lists what you
can do next at its foot, and picking one does it: post the comments, leave
findings out or change a level, reset that. A conversation used for a review
is named after its PR instead of staying "New session", and several texts of
setup say more exactly what they mean. The reviewer, verifier and
comment-planning instructions are those of 0.4.3, and no setting is new.

## What changed

- **The next step is in the panel.** A receipt ends with the commands for the
  next step, but the panel shows the report or preview, so those commands had
  to be found in the conversation and typed. After a preview the panel lists
  them in one row at its foot, where reading ends, and the row stays in place
  while the text scrolls:

  ```text
  [p] Post 4 comments…   [a] Adjust findings…   [u] Reset adjustments
  ```

  Click one, or press its key while the panel has the keyboard; the keys are
  drawn dim while they would only type a letter into the prompt. A label that
  ends in `…` asks before anything is sent. **Reset adjustments** is there
  once something was adjusted.
- **Posting asks first.** The question's first row is "No, post nothing", so
  a key pressed twice posts nothing.
- **Findings are adjusted from a list.** The findings are listed with how
  each is published now. Pick one to leave it out or to choose its level, and
  apply every change at once from the foot of the list (**apply**, `ctrl+s`),
  which stays in view however long the list is; the preview is then planned
  again and shown from its beginning. No finding ID is typed.
- **They send the command you would type.** Each sends `/pr-comment` with
  the ID of the review the panel shows, to the session on screen, and AZPR
  takes it like a typed command: the same checks, the same `STARTED` notice
  and receipt. The panel sends nothing by itself and never a prompt, and the
  steps are there only for the notice that happened last. After a review that
  no preview follows by itself (`afterReview: none`), the row offers
  **Preview comments** (`c`) instead of posting.
- **Nothing is posted that you have not read.** A click on one of the steps
  leaves the keyboard with the prompt, and a step is picked only by pressing
  and letting go of the left button on it: not by letting go after the
  pointer has left it, and not by the end of a selection of text (which also
  no longer opens a session from its row, or closes the panel, as it did
  since 0.4.2). An answer is acted on only while the
  panel still shows what you answered for: if the preview is planned again,
  another session comes on screen or the panel is closed while a question is
  open, nothing is sent and the panel says so. Each command the panel sends
  also says which preview and adjustments it was picked for (`--seen`), and
  AZPR refuses it when they have changed somewhere the panel was not told
  of, such as the review's own session or another client. A preview that
  another command adjusted, planned again or posted while its own run was
  ending is no longer shown as a preview: that run ends with the status
  `REPLACED`, and the other command's receipt is the one to read.
- **A session that has answered is `finished`.** While a review ran, a
  reviewer session that had answered was shown as `idle`, OpenCode's word for
  a session at rest, which read like a fault. It is `finished` now, until the
  run's receipt names its result.
- **A conversation is named after its PR.** OpenCode names a conversation when
  its own model first runs there, which an AZPR command never makes it do. A
  check or a review now names a conversation nobody named, for example
  `AZPR: PR #123 (repository)`. A name that is there stays. OpenCode has no
  rename that applies only to an unnamed conversation, so AZPR follows the
  renames OpenCode reports: a name that you or OpenCode's model give in that
  very moment is

releases.name: v0.4.3 — Setup in the terminal UI
releases.body:
# Azure DevOps PR Review for OpenCode — 0.4.3

`/pr-setup` now sets AZPR up inside OpenCode's terminal UI: it asks for your
organization, a proxy if your network needs one, your token and a model,
checks the token with Azure DevOps and saves it in a file only you can read.
A first setup needs no restart. And after a review, the next thing you say in
the same conversation no longer costs one model request per AZPR notice. The
reviewer, verifier and comment-planning instructions are those of 0.4.2, and
no setting is new.

## What changed

- **Setup in dialogs.** A first setup used to mean creating the PAT file by
  hand in a terminal, typing a model ID, editing JSON for a proxy and
  restarting the OpenCode service. In the terminal UI, type `/pr-setup` and
  answer four questions: the organization (its name, or the URL of a pull
  request), a proxy (Enter skips it), the token, and a model from OpenCode's
  list.
- **The token stays hidden and is checked.** You paste it into a field that
  shows only how many characters it holds. AZPR asks Azure DevOps once
  whether it works for your organization and says what was refused: the
  token, the organization, or the way there. It is then saved alone in a
  file only you can read (mode 600): a file made for it,
  `pat-<organization>` in AZPR's directory, or the token file your settings
  name already for that organization. It is in no conversation, notice or
  log.
- **What could make setup fail is asked first.** The proxy comes before the
  token, because the token is checked over the network; after a proxy, the
  CA certificate file of a company that inspects HTTPS. If Azure DevOps still
  cannot be reached, the proxy or the CA file can be set right there and the
  same token tried again.
- **No restart after a first setup.** The review commands work at once, with
  the dialogs and with `/pr-setup --organization … --model …` alike. (A
  second project directory that the OpenCode service had already opened
  without settings still needs one, and says so.)
- **Settings as a list.** With settings in place, `/pr-setup` shows them with
  their values: organization, token, proxy, CA certificate file, the review,
  quick and deep models, output language, what follows a review, the report
  in the conversation, progress notices, the review panel and debug records.
  Choose one to change it. A change to settings that are in use takes effect
  after `opencode service restart`, and the list says so. Posting comments
  without a preview asks once more. Another organization asks for a token
  of its own: a saved token belongs to the organization it was checked for
  and is never sent to another one. The new token gets a new file, and
  AZPR says where the earlier one still is.
- **Options for one setting each**, for clients without the dialogs and for
  scripts: `--proxy`, `--ca-file`, `--review-model`, `--quick-model`,
  `--deep-model`, `--language`, `--after-review`, `--report`, `--progress`,
  `--panel` and `--debug`, without `--replace`.
- **A prompt after a review costs one request, not one per notice.** AZPR
  tells the conversation what a run does with notices (`STARTED`,
  `PROGRESS`, the receipts). They wait in the conversation's inbox and start
  no response of its model. Until now, when you then prompted that
  conversation, OpenCode 2.3.0 answered your prompt and after it gave each
  waiting notice a turn of the conversation's model: about eight more
  requests after a review with its comment preview, each carrying the whole
  conversation. The conversation's model now reads all waiting notices
  together with your prompt, in one request. In the terminal fixture, a
  prompt after 16 notices made 17 requests before and makes 1 now.

The dialogs need OpenCode's terminal UI. Other clients, such as the desktop
app, show `/pr-setup`'s instructions as before and take its options. The
dialogs only ask: the plugin's server part checks every answer, writes the
files and is the only part that c

releases.name: v0.4.2 — A terminal panel for reports and previews
releases.body:
# Azure DevOps PR Review for OpenCode — 0.4.2

This release adds a panel to OpenCode's terminal UI. OpenCode shows what a
plugin tells a conversation as plain text, so AZPR's report and comment
preview appeared as Markdown source, and since 0.4.1 a reviewer session had to
be picked from OpenCode's session list. The panel shows the newest report or
preview rendered and lists the sessions of the review, each a click away.

Two smaller changes come with it. A PR that was completed or abandoned, such
as one merged before its review was commented on, now takes comments like an
active one. And a new version writes the settings it brings into your settings
file, at their defaults, so each is there to change.

The reviewer, verifier and comment-planning instructions are those of 0.4.1.
One setting is new: `terminalPanel`.

## What changed

- **The report and the preview are rendered.** A panel beside the conversation
  shows the newest report or comment preview with headings, emphasis, lists,
  code and tables. The report of a review is followed by the preview once one
  is planned, and by the saved preview again after `/pr-comment --show`. A
  check's table is shown there too.
- **The review's sessions are in the panel.** While a review runs, each of its
  sessions is a row with its state. Afterwards the rows are the sessions that
  still exist, first the one that holds the report. Click a row to open that
  session; OpenCode opens it in a tab, and the panel is there again when you
  return to the conversation.
- **It opens by itself and leaves the keyboard with the prompt.** The panel
  opens when a review or a comment run starts and when a report or preview
  arrives, in the conversation on screen, so the next command can be typed
  while the report is in view. `/pr-panel`, its only command, shows and hides
  it. To have it open only when you ask, set this in AZPR's settings and
  restart the OpenCode service:

  ```json
  "terminalPanel": "manual"
  ```

- **Keys.** A click inside the panel gives it the keyboard: the arrow keys or
  `j` and `k`, Page Up and Page Down, Home and End scroll, and Escape or `q`
  closes it.
- **A narrow terminal is left alone.** With fewer than 108 columns OpenCode
  shows a panel in place of the conversation. There the panel does not open by
  itself; it says that something is ready, and `/pr-panel` shows it full
  screen.
- **The panel only reads.** It reads AZPR's notices in the conversation, the
  report queued to the review's session, and which sessions belong to the run.
  It sends no prompt, starts no review and posts nothing; `/pr-comment
  --publish` is still a command you type.

The panel is part of OpenCode's terminal UI. Other clients, such as the
desktop app, do not load it and show AZPR's notices as before. The
[README](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.4.2/README.md#terminal-panel)
describes it.

- **Comments on a completed or abandoned PR.** `/pr-comment --publish` refused
  a PR that was no longer active, so a PR merged before its review was
  commented on could be reviewed but not commented on. The PR's status no
  longer stops a publication, typed or automatic, and the receipt names it
  (`Publication (VERIFIED=3); the PR is completed:`). A changed source commit
  is still refused, and nothing is posted twice. `/pr-check` shows such a PR
  with a WARNING instead of `NOT_READY`.
- **New settings arrive in your settings file.** When OpenCode first loads a
  version that brings a setting, AZPR writes it into your settings file at
  its default; until now only a source installation did. The defaults written
  are the ones that applied anyway, so AZPR behaves as before. Your values
  and their order stay, the file is written with two-space indentation and
  readable by its owner only (mode 600), and `/pr-check` lists what was
  added. A settings file that is a symbolic link, invalid or switched off
  is left as it is, and `/pr-check` then names the setti
